summary: Added session resume to the codex adapter. CodexDriver now declares supportsResume=true, captures thread_id from thread.started as StageResult.session_id, and honors DriveOpts.resumeSession by probing `codex exec --help` (memoized cliCanResume) for a resume subcommand: if present it drives `codex exec resume <id> …`, otherwise it runs a fresh context and sets StageResult.resume_unsupported. buildExecArgs gained an optional resumeSessionId param that assembles the `exec resume <id>` invocation (fresh path unchanged). engine.ts logs a distinct session_resume_unsupported run event (separate from the GC'd-session session_resume_failed) when result.resume_unsupported is set, so the fallback is explicit in the run-event log rather than silent. Added a resume_unsupported field to StageResult in types.ts. Extended the stub-driven adapter tests to cover session_id capture, the exec-resume arg shape, resume-with-session, and the explicit-fallback path.

Fixed the MUST-FIX: safe-perms (skipPermissions:false) resume was building `codex exec resume ... --sandbox read-only`, which codex-cli 0.144.1 rejects (exit 2, 'unexpected argument --sandbox' — verified against the real CLI). buildExecArgs now emits --sandbox read-only on the fresh path only (else if !resumeSessionId), and run() only resumes under full-auto perms — a safe-perms resume can't pin the read-only sandbox, so it falls back to a fresh read-only context and sets resume_unsupported (preserving the guardrail, never emitting args codex rejects). Broadened the resume_unsupported doc to cover this second reason. Made the test stub reject resume+--sandbox like real codex and added two regression tests; both were verified to fail on the reverted code and pass with the fix.
